title: Indexing and Metadata Audit for 5 Core Pages
description:
Audience: Developers and tech students landing on the platform via direct search or social links.

Links: Google Search Console Overview, Schema.org Documentation

Tone: Technical, clear, and direct.

Deadline: 48 hours (2 days solo).

Definition of "Done": Meta titles, meta descriptions, open graph tags, and primary target keywords are audited and updated for 5 main pages, with sitemap resubmission confirmed in Google Search Console.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Audit and fix the five pages in the repo: implement the metadata in code, not in a report
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Do the audit and the fix in one pass using the open-source zedu-fe repo (Next.js). For each of the five core pages, read the current layout/page Metadata API output, log the before state (title, description, OG tags, canonical, index status), then write the corrected metadata in code with one distinct buyer-intent keyword per page, and verify the after state by fetching the live DOM and Open Graph preview. Deliverable: a five-row before/after table with the commit that made each change, so the sitemap resubmission in Search Console shows a genuinely improved site instead of a spreadsheet of recommendations. Distinct from audit-first approaches: the same effort produces merged fixes, not just a findings list.

upvotes.reason: On the pages this goal is about, "Audit and fix the five pages in the repo: implement the metadata in code, not in a report" is the kind of fix that can be verified against the live site after delivery, so it either moved the number or it did not. it produces something checkable rather than an opinion, so the goal either moved or it did not.

The goal says metadata is 'audited and updated', and this is the only idea that puts the fix in the repo rather than in a report. Reading the Next.js Metadata API output, writing the corrected metadata, and proving it in the live DOM with a commit per row gives the goal a mergeable result and a real before/after record. I back it.

Focuses on actual implementation rather than duplicate audit reports, directly solving search indexing and title hierarchy in the codebase.
Fixing the metadata in the code in the same pass removes the report-then-forget failure mode, and the before-and-after log per page lets anyone reviewing the diff check the change themselves.

downvotes.reason: The goal already has an accepted five-page audit approach that explicitly continues through owner-approved changes and post-change verification, plus an accepted reuse-first approach coordinating existing title, description and sitemap tasks. This proposal repeats that scope while claiming the others end at a report. Writing a patch belongs as a task in the accepted approach; a second independent metadata rewrite risks conflicting edits. Reuse the approved metadata and add the implementation task there, with deployment and Search Console access as explicit dependencies.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Audit five pages against buyer search intent, then verify metadata and indexing
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Start with the five agreed pages and record each current title, description, canonical URL, open-graph preview, target query and index status. Match each page to one distinct search intent using real buyer language, then draft metadata that accurately reflects the live page and avoids overlapping another page. Check title and description lengths, social previews, canonical tags and sitemap inclusion; after the owner approves changes, resubmit the sitemap in Search Console and attach the before/after register with screenshots or exported checks. This gives the team a traceable baseline and confirms the changes are visible to search engines, rather than treating metadata edits as complete without checking indexing.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Reuse the title and description work already under way, add the Open Graph checks, and get a real sitemap before resubmitting
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Much of this is already in progress under other goals: one title pattern under 60 characters, unique meta descriptions under 155, and a real robots.txt and sitemap.xml each have accepted approaches and open tasks. Two facts shape the plan (checked 22 Oct 2026): zedu.chat/sitemap.xml returns the HTML page, not a sitemap, so there's nothing to resubmit in Search Console until the sitemap task ships; and every page's share image is served from a 'telexprodbucket' path. Plan: 1) for the 5 core pages (home, pricing, about, a product page, a solutions page), record the live title, description, canonical, og:title, og:description, og:image and Twitter card, and take the new titles and descriptions from the existing goals' approved work rather than writing a second set; 2) add the missing Open Graph and Twitter fields and a target keyword per page, checked with a social preview tool; 3) once the real sitemap is live, submit it in Search Console and record each page's indexing status with the date. Tasks: 5-page metadata register with OG fixes (SEO), Search Console submission and index check (SEO).

pendingIdeas.title: Make every audited page self-canonical before the metadata is rewritten: three live pages currently canonicalise to the homepage
pendingIdeas.description:
Problem, verified on 22 Oct 2026: /resources, /policy and /terms-of-service all serve rel=canonical https://zedu.chat. The cause is the homepage layout metadata (src/app/(homepage)/layout.tsx, lines 57-58) applying canonical "/" to every child route that does not override it. /pricing and /download already override it correctly, which proves the pattern. Any title or description rewritten on an audited page inherits the wrong canonical and sends search engines to the homepage, so the metadata work cannot pay off until this is fixed.

Approach: (1) add alternates.canonical to each public route, or move the default out of the (homepage) layout into the homepage page itself, then deploy to staging; (2) crawl the full public route inventory - the 17 pages already listed in the sitemap work - and record the served canonical for each; (3) assert canonical == page URL, flagging the three current failures and any route that still inherits; (4) add that assertion as a release check so a new page cannot ship inheriting the homepage canonical.

Why it fits: this goal audits indexing and metadata on core pages; a non-self canonical makes every other metadata item on that page inert for indexing. The fix is in shared metadata code, so it corrects all three pages at once and prevents recurrence.

Done when: a dated 17-row crawl shows every public page's canonical equals its own URL, the three inherited cases are gone, and the check runs in the release process with a failing example recorded.

Measured: canonical-equals-self count before and after (today 3 of 17 fail), and after four weeks, the number of audited pages indexed under their own URL in Search Console rather than folded into the homepage. No ranking claim is made from the code change alone.

upvotes.reason: On the pages this goal is about, "Make every audited page self-canonical before the metadata is rewritten: three live pages currently canonicalise to the homepage" is the kind of fix that can be verified against the live site after delivery, so it either moved the number or it did not. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

The cause is identified rather than guessed: layout metadata setting canonical to the homepage for every child route, with three live pages still affected. Fixing that one place and then rewriting titles is the correct order.

I checked this myself on 22 Oct 2026: /resources, /policy and /terms-of-service all serve rel=canonical https://zedu.chat, while /pricing, /download and /about correctly point at themselves. The claim and the cause are right. No title or description rewritten on those three pages can pay off until this is fixed, so it belongs before the metadata work.
